question: For a four-leg intersection evaluated under the one-year Crash Experience signal warrant, what crash thresholds apply and what two additional categories of conditions must also be satisfied?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under the one-year evaluation of Warrant 7 (Crash Experience), the number of reported angle crashes and pedestrian crashes (all severities), or fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes, within a 1-year period must equal or exceed the applicable threshold numbers in Table 4C-2. In addition to the crash-history condition, two other categories of conditions must be satisfied: (A) an adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce crash frequency, and (C) a vehicular volume condition applying to each of any 8 hours of an average day. Note that the specific numeric threshold values from Table 4C-2 for a four-leg intersection are not contained in the evidence provided (only an isolated fragment reading "2 or more" appears, without sufficient context to attribute it to a specific cell of the table), so the exact four-leg numbers cannot be stated. Guidance (recommended): - "The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that all of the following criteria are met: A. Adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce the crash frequency; and B. At least one of the following conditions applies to the reported crash history..." - For the one-year evaluation: "1. The number of reported angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total angle crashes and pedestrian crashes (all severities); or 2. The number of reported fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes..." - The third required category is a volume condition: "C. For each of any 8 hours of an average day, the ve[hicular volume...]" (the provision is truncated in the evidence, but it establishes an 8-hour vehicular volume requirement as an additional criterion). - The evidence fragment "2 or more" (Section 4C.08, p.662) appears to be a threshold value from the warrant's tables, but its context (which table, severity category, or intersection configuration) is not provided. Citations: - Section 4C.08 Guidance §2 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Guidance §1 (p.662)
gold_answer: The thresholds are at least 5 all-severity angle/pedestrian crashes or at least 3 fatal-and-injury angle/pedestrian crashes. In addition, an adequate trial of alternatives must have failed, and the applicable 80-percent vehicular-volume or pedestrian-volume condition must be met for the required hours.
